nodes.summary: The set of atoms (propositional variables) occurring in a modal formula.
nodes.title: Atoms of a modal formula

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$ and a modal formula $\varphi$, the iterated box $\Box^k \varphi$ is defined by $\Box^0 \varphi = \varphi$ and $\Box^{k+1} \varphi = \Box\,\Box^k \varphi$.
nodes.title: Iterated box

nodes.summary: Negative and positive modal formulas are defined by simultaneous recursion: no atom is negative, $\bot$ is negative, $\varphi \to \psi$ is negative if $\varphi$ is positive and $\psi$ is negative, and $\Box\varphi$ is negative if $\varphi$ is negative.
nodes.title: Negative modal formulas

nodes.summary: Positive and negative modal formulas are defined by simultaneous recursion: every atom is positive, $\bot$ is positive, $\varphi \to \psi$ is positive if $\varphi$ is negative and $\psi$ is positive, and $\Box\varphi$ is positive if $\varphi$ is positive.
nodes.title: Positive modal formulas

nodes.summary: The Sahlqvist antecedents form the smallest class of modal formulas that contains every boxed atom $\Box^k p$ (an atom $p$ under $k \ge 0$ boxes) and every negative formula, and is closed under $\wedge$, $\vee$ and $\Diamond$.
nodes.title: Sahlqvist antecedents

nodes.summary: For every atom $p$, the instance $p \to \Box\Diamond p$ of the B axiom is a Sahlqvist formula: its antecedent $p$ is a boxed atom with zero boxes and its consequent $\Box\Diamond p$ is positive.
nodes.title: The B axiom is a Sahlqvist formula

nodes.summary: A modal formula is a Sahlqvist implication if it is an implication $\alpha \to \beta$ whose antecedent $\alpha$ is a Sahlqvist antecedent and whose consequent $\beta$ is a positive formula.
nodes.title: Sahlqvist implications

nodes.summary: The Sahlqvist formulas form the smallest class of modal formulas that contains every Sahlqvist implication, is closed under $\wedge$ and $\Box$, and contains $\varphi \vee \psi$ whenever $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are Sahlqvist formulas with no atom in common.
nodes.title: Sahlqvist formulas

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
